title: The median: order first, then find the middle
skill: Find the median of 5–10 whole numbers (order first; halfway between the two middle values for an even count).

concept: The median is the middle value once the data are IN ORDER: half the values are below it, half above.
With an even number of values there are two middle values; the median is halfway between them.
explanation.visualNote: Reuses the table visual to show the ordered list; crossing off from both ends is the family's own cross_off alternative.

workedExamples.prompt: Find the median of these numbers: 75, 14, 80, 65, 66.
lines: In order: 14, 65, 66, 75, 80 (5 values)
The middle one is the 3rd value: 66

workedExamples.prompt: Find the median of these numbers: 27, 83, 21, 62, 73, 63, 34, 52, 80, 90.
lines: The two middle values are the 5th and 6th: 62 and 63; halfway: (62 + 63) ÷ 2 = 62.5
familyExplainSteps: The two middle values are 62 and 63: (62 + 63) ÷ 2 = 62.5

hints: Write them from smallest to largest.

alternativeExplanation.title: Line up by height
text: Line the numbers up from smallest to largest, like children by height.
The child in the middle of the line is the median; with two in the middle, take halfway.

alternativeMethods.name: Cross off from both ends
example: cross off smallest and largest repeatedly; left: 66

whatWentWrong: In "Find the median of these numbers: 59, 50, 87, 86, 81.", one wrong answer is 87.
The middle number of the list as given was taken. Put the numbers in order first.
The middle of the list only means something once the list is in order.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check: in the order given the middle is 87; in order it is 81. Reorder the same data and the 'middle' would change, so it cannot be a fact about the data.
solvedCorrectly: The middle one is the 3rd value: 81

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)

whatWentWrong: In "Find the median of these numbers: 21, 74, 25, 41, 80, 81, 64, 47, 62.", one wrong answer is 55.
The mean was worked out. The median is the middle value once the numbers are in order.
The mean shares the total equally; the median is the middle value in order. They are different averages.
screens.counterCheck: Check: the total 495 shared equally among 9 values is 55 (the mean); in order, 21, 25, 41, 47, 62, 64, 74, 80, 81, the middle value is different.
solvedCorrectly: The middle one is the 5th value: 62

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)

whatWentWrong: In "Find the median of these numbers: 66, 58, 75, 81, 14, 95.", one wrong answer is 66 or 75.
With 6 numbers there are two middle numbers (66 and 75); the median is halfway between them.
With an even number of values there are two middle values: take halfway between them.
screens.counterCheck: Check: 6 values have no single middle; the 3rd and 4th values, 66 and 75, share the middle, so the median is halfway: 70.5.
solvedCorrectly: The two middle values are the 3rd and 4th: 66 and 75; halfway: (66 + 75) ÷ 2 = 70.5
